info.title: Mirai Voice API
info.description: The v2 API for voice agents, calls, campaigns, phone numbers and speech. Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…`. Generated from the API's own contract and its Postman collection.

servers.description: Sandbox: trial workspaces, before your company goes live
Production: workspaces that have gone live

tags.name: Agents
tags.description:
An agent is what a call runs: its prompt (or a node flow, see the Flows section), voice, language and limits. Write it once and dial it as often as you like; each call fills in its own `variables`.

Every save creates a new revision. You can read old revisions, roll back to one, and publish a draft when it is ready. None of the requests here place a call or charge your wallet.

tags.name: Calls
tags.description:
Place a call, follow it while it runs, then read what happened: the transcript, the recording, the post-call analysis.

`POST /v2/calls` answers before the phone rings, with an id. Everything after that is about that id. Every call has a live event stream, phone calls included, so your own dashboard can show a call as it happens. Live control works on browser calls (`channel: "web"`) and realtime sessions only; a phone call answers it with `400 unsupported_channel`.

tags.name: Flows
tags.description:
A node-based agent runs the call as a graph of steps. Each node has its own instructions, and the agent moves to the next node when a transition's condition is met, so a call with branches (wrong person, not now, reschedule) stays easy to follow and to change.

The usual path: draft a graph from a brief or from recordings of your real calls, check it, test it with simulated calls, then save it on an agent. Drafting, transcribing and testing use AI models and charge your wallet; checking, saving and reading are free.

Full guide: https://docs.miraiminds.co/v2/node-agents

tags.name: Tools and secrets
tags.description:
Connect your own APIs to an agent. A tool runs at one of three moments:

* `pre_call`, before dialling: fetch context for the greeting, or skip the call.
* `on_call`, when the agent decides to use it mid-conversation: look something up, book something.
* `post_call`, after the call has settled: send the outcome to your CRM, schedule a call back.

The order here is the order you'd use them in: see what's available, store your credential as a secret, add a tool, test it against your endpoint, then read each call's tool runs. Tools themselves cost nothing extra.

Tool definitions use Mirai's own templates, like `{{ args.date }}` and `{{ secrets.crm_key }}`.

A definition that doesn't validate comes back as a list, so you can fix everything at once: `{"error": "invalid_tools", "details": [{"path", "message"}]}`. Everything else uses the usual `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description:
Call a whole list with one agent. Upload contacts, say which days and hours the campaign may ring, and start it. From then on it dials by itself: it paces itself, waits overnight, retries calls that didn't connect, skips numbers on your do-not-call list, and pauses itself when its budget or your wallet runs out.

Campaign calls are ordinary calls. They show up in `GET /v2/calls`, send the same `call.*` webhooks and bill the same per-minute rate. In a sandbox workspace every campaign runs and bills at T5 (₹5 a minute), whatever tier you ask for.

Money on a campaign is in **paise**: `"budget_paise": 50000` is ₹500.

The requests run top to bottom: create saves `campaign_id`, and the rest use it. Starting a campaign rings every contact on it, so put numbers you're allowed to call in the bodies first.

tags.name: Do-not-call list
tags.description:
Numbers your campaigns will never dial. The list covers every campaign in the workspace, including ones that are already running: it's checked at the moment a contact is about to be called, so a number added mid-campaign is skipped from then on. A skipped contact stays in its campaign as `suppressed` and costs nothing.

It doesn't apply to single calls placed with `POST /v2/calls`; check the list yourself before those if you need to. It's your own list, not the national DND register, and adding a number here doesn't meet your DND obligations.

tags.name: Phone numbers
tags.description:
The numbers your agents answer. Each one comes from the **Telephony** section:

* **Rented from Mirai.** Once the rental is active, the number shows up here by itself (`ownership: managed`).
* **From your own Plivo account.** Connect the account in Telephony, list its numbers, then bring one here with [Import a Plivo number](/api-reference/phone-numbers/import-a-plivo-number) (`ownership: customer`). Plivo keeps billing you for it.

After that it's two steps, in this order: [Assign an agent](/api-reference/phone-numbers/assign-an-agent) (who answers), then [Turn on incoming calls](/api-reference/phone-numbers/turn-on-incoming-calls). `state` is `imported` until calls are on and `ready` after; `error` means the last attempt to turn calls on failed, and `setup_error` says why.

Every change sends the number's current `version`, and each change raises it by one. If you're not sure what it is, read the number first; a stale version is a 409 `conflict` and changes nothing.

To call out from one of your numbers, place a call with `phone_number_id` set to its id once it is `ready` (Indian destinations only). Calls on your numbers are billed like any other call.

Every number also says how it is doing in `health`: `state` is `active`, `warming` (its first week, at half its pool's pace), `resting`, `cooling` (rested three times in a day; waits for you) or `retired`, with this hour's attempts and seven days of answers. You can rest, resume and retire your own numbers; a resting or retired number still answers calls to it.

tags.name: Phone pools
tags.description:
A pool is a group of your own phone numbers that a campaign, an agent or a single call can ring from. Each call takes the number best placed for it: a number a contact has already been rung from stays theirs on a retry, numbers in the contact's own circle come first, and the pool's pace (`max_per_hour`, per number) is held across every campaign and API call at once. A number whose answers drop well below its pool-mates' rests on its own for 45 minutes.

Point a campaign at a pool with `pool_id` on [Create a campaign](/api-reference/campaigns/create-a-campaign), an agent with `calls_from: {"pool_id": …}`, or one call with `pool_id` on [Place a call](/api-reference/calls/place-a-call). `pool_id` and `phone_number_id` never go together. With nothing chosen, calls come from the agent's setting, then the pool marked `default_for_campaigns`, then the Mirai shared line. A call's `calls_from_source` is `pool` (with `pool_id`) when a pool picked its number.

A single call on a pool whose numbers are all resting or at their pace this hour answers 409 `pool_busy` with `Retry-After`; one with no number that can call, 409 `pool_unavailable`. A campaign doesn't fail: it waits and carries on.

`purpose` is what the calls are for: `outreach` (promotional), `reminders`, `support` or `other`. It sets the starting pace: 40 an hour for support, 60 otherwise. Pools are free; numbers are billed as numbers.

tags.name: Telephony
tags.description:
Getting a phone number for your agent. There are two ways, and a workspace can use both.

**1. Rent a number from Mirai.** ₹500 a month, paid as ₹1,500 from your wallet every three months, renewing until you turn it off. Indian numbers need a business verification that Plivo approves once: read the requirements, submit your details and documents, then refresh until it's `accepted`. After that: search, quote, rent. The rented number appears in **Phone numbers** by itself.

**2. Connect your own Plivo account.** Plivo keeps billing you directly. Connect it with your Auth ID and Auth Token, list the numbers it owns, and bring one over with [Import a Plivo number](/api-reference/phone-numbers/import-a-plivo-number). A Plivo main account can also rent new numbers through the same search → quote → rent requests, with its connection id as `account`.

Either way you finish in **Phone numbers**: assign the agent that answers, then turn on incoming calls.

The last two requests verify your own phone, so the workspace can ring it from Mirai's shared test number (test calls are placed from the Numbers page in the console).

Indian (+91) numbers only for now. If phone numbers aren't available on the host you're calling, every request here answers 503 `telephony_unavailable`.

tags.name: Transcriptions
tags.description: Turn a recorded call (or any recording) into a transcript with speakers and timestamps. Hindi, English, Gujarati and mixed speech are written the way they were spoken, never translated. ₹18 per hour of audio; failed and degraded jobs are free.

tags.name: Speech to text
tags.description:
Speech to text in ten languages, two ways: send one recording and get its text back in the same request ([Transcribe a recording](/api-reference/speech-to-text/transcribe-a-recording)), or stream live audio over one WebSocket per call and read partial transcripts while people speak, then one final transcript per utterance. Language codes: hi-IN, en-IN, gu-IN, mr-IN, pa-IN, bn-IN, ta-IN, te-IN, kn-IN or ml-IN.

`wss://sandbox.voice.miraiminds.co/v1/audio/transcriptions/stream?language_code=hi-IN&encoding=mulaw&sample_rate=8000&endpointing=manual`

(`wss://prod.voice.miraiminds.co` once your company has gone live), with the header `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_YOUR_API_KEY`. 8 or 16 kHz, 16-bit PCM, μ-law or A-law. A browser uses `?token=` from [Mint stream tokens](/api-reference/speech-to-text/mint-stream-tokens) instead, because it cannot set headers on a WebSocket.

Send JSON text frames: `{"event": "speech_start"}`, then `{"event": "audio_input", "audio": "<base64 audio>"}` as the audio arrives, then `{"event": "speech_end"}`; `{"event": "end"}` closes the session. You receive `session.begin` first, `transcript.partial` while an utterance is open, exactly one `transcript.final` per utterance, and `session.end` with `audio_seconds_billed` and `cost_paise`.

Every event, both endpointing modes, limits and errors: https://docs.miraiminds.co/v2/stt-quickstart

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Get call events at your own HTTPS URL, signed, retried and kept for 30 days.

1. [Create a destination](/api-reference/webhooks/create-a-destination) with your URL. Save the `signing_secret` from that answer: it is shown once.
2. [Subscribe a destination to events](/api-reference/webhooks/subscribe-a-destination-to-events), for one agent or the whole workspace. `call.completed` arrives when a call ends; `call.processing.completed` when the recording, transcript, results and post-call tools have all settled.
3. [Send a test event](/api-reference/webhooks/send-a-test-event). It is a real POST to your URL with made-up call data and `test: true`. No call is placed.

Every request carries `X-Mirai-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of `<unix>.<raw body>`, and `X-Mirai-Signed-With`, which names the secret that signed it. A destination's requests are signed with its own Destination secret; the `webhook_url` you pass when creating a call is signed with your Call webhook secret, the one shown with your API keys. A URL that is both gets each event once, with one secret. Delivery is at least once, so keep each event `id` and skip ones you've already handled.

Changes send the resource's current `revision` (`if_revision`); a stale one is a 409 and changes nothing. Until the webhook release reaches your workspace these routes answer 404. The same settings are in the console under Webhooks, and on each agent in Agent Studio.

post.description:
Creates an agent. Nothing is dialled and nothing is charged.

`name`, `system_prompt`, `first_message` and `language` are required. Everything else has a working default, and the response shows every default it filled in. `{{name}}`-style placeholders in the prompts are filled from each call's `variables`.

`voice.voice_id` must be a voice that `GET /v2/voices` lists. Anything else is a 400 that names the voices you can use. `secondary_languages` are other languages your callers may switch to; speech recognition listens for them too.

Turn on the `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe. Sending the same key again returns the agent it first created (200, with `Idempotent-Replay: true`) instead of a second agent. The same key with a different body is a 409.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Up to 255 characters. The same key within 24 hours replays the first answer and creates nothing new. Build it from your own record, such as `order-8842-reminder-1`.

patch.description:
Send only the fields you are changing. Each save is a new revision.

Nested objects (`voice`, `end_call`, `voicemail`, `background_sound`, `analysis`) are replaced whole, and so are the `tools` list and the `flow` graph, so send the complete object. `behavior` is the exception: it merges field by field, and `behavior.pass_through` (words that never interrupt the agent) replaces the whole list you send.

To refuse a stale edit, add `"if_revision"` with the revision you read. If someone saved the agent in between, you get a 409 and nothing changes.

`{"archived": true}` stops new calls without deleting the agent, and `{"archived": false}` brings it back. Changes apply from the next call; calls already queued or running keep the version they started with.

post.description:
Fills the agent's prompts with a set of `variables` and returns the text a call would start with. Nothing is saved, dialled or charged, so it is a cheap way to check your variables before a campaign.

Add `changes` (any fields `PATCH` accepts) to preview an edit before you save it. If the agent has an `input_schema`, the values are checked against it and its defaults are filled in. Without one, every value must be a string, and a placeholder with no value renders empty.

analysis.description: Replace the whole analysis block. Omit output_schema to remove structured extraction. Requires enabled=true to run.

enabled.description: Run the analysis after every call that connected; a call that never connected is skipped (not_connected). Default false. On the T1 plan, your workspace's insights setting decides this for each call instead.

output_schema.description: The shape of analysis.data: a root object schema from the documented bounded subset. Nested nodes use the same keywords; the server validates depth, node count and keyword/type compatibility. The model's data must satisfy it before the result is published. Not a template: placeholders are not rendered here.

additionalProperties.description: Nested schema node; same supported subset.

prompt.description: What the analysis should summarise or extract, in your words: the instruction the model reads beside the transcript. At most 2000 characters. {{variable}} placeholders render with the same rules as system_prompt: the call's variables (for example {{customer_name}}) and pre-call tool outputs as {{tool_name.key}}. A placeholder with no value renders empty. For example: Write the summary in {{summary_language}}.

success_criteria.description: How to decide success: true, false, or null when the conversation does not show it. At most 2000 characters. {{variable}} placeholders render with the same rules as system_prompt: the call's variables (for example {{customer_name}}) and pre-call tool outputs as {{tool_name.key}}. A placeholder with no value renders empty.

archived.description: Archive to block new calls; false restores availability subject to draft validation. Accepted call snapshots remain unchanged.

behavior.description: How the agent takes turns with the caller, and whether it knows the date. Unlike other nested blocks, PATCH merges it field by field: omitted fields keep their current value and {} changes nothing; a sent pass_through replaces the whole list. null resets it to the defaults (interruptions normal, adaptive_interruptions true, pass_through [], date_awareness true).

adaptive_interruptions.description: Turn-taking, on by default. The agent decides when the caller has finished speaking: it waits through mid-thought pauses with a short "hmm", ignores quieter voices in the background (someone else in the room), and picks up a line it was cut off on if the interruption turns out to be nothing. Turn it off for fixed rules only: the interruptions setting decides how many words cut the agent off, and pass_through words never do.

date_awareness.description: Date awareness, on by default. The agent knows today's date in the call's timezone (the campaign's, else India), and whenever the caller names a day ("Saturday", "शनिवार", "15 तारीख", "कल", "next Monday", "15 November") it is told the exact date before it replies, so it never works out a date or a weekday itself. A day that does not exist (31 November) is flagged to the agent, and each resolved date is a row in the agent's Logs (prompt). Turn it off only if your own prompt or tools supply dates differently.

interruptions.description: How easily the caller can cut the agent off while it speaks. easy: one word or about 0.5 s of speech; normal (the default, and the behaviour before this setting existed): two words or about 0.7 s; firm: three words or about 1.2 s; never: the agent always finishes its line, and what the caller said is answered right after. Acknowledgements (haan, ji, ok, hmm and your pass_through words) never interrupt at any setting; a stop word (stop, ruko) interrupts at every setting except never. On a flow agent a node's own allow_interrupt false still applies; never makes every node non-interruptible. Trimmed and lower-cased; any other value, including an empty string, is 400.

pass_through.description: Your own words that never interrupt the agent, such as "theek", "achha" or "bilkul". They are added to the built-in acknowledgements (haan, ji, ok, hmm and their equivalents), which always pass through; a reply made only of these words does not stop the agent. Applies whether adaptive_interruptions is on or off. Each entry is literal text, never a pattern: Unicode-normalised (NFC), trimmed and inner spaces collapsed to one, then 1-40 characters and at most 4 words. Duplicates are removed ignoring case, keeping the first spelling and the order; at most 30 entries. Sent, it replaces the whole list; [] or null clears it. Anything else is 400 invalid_request naming behavior.pass_through.

booking.description: The agent's booking window: which days a caller may book. With date awareness on, every day a caller names is marked as bookable or not before the agent replies (after the window, a closed weekday or date, already past), the agent is told the window in its prompt and offered the nearest bookable day, so it never confirms a day you cannot take. Absent when not set. A PATCH replaces the whole block (omitted fields take their defaults); null removes it.

closed_dates.description: Single days that cannot be booked, such as holidays, as YYYY-MM-DD. Saved unique and sorted; at most 100.

closed_weekdays.description: Days of the week that cannot be booked, lower case. Saved unique and in week order; closing all seven is 400.

same_day.description: Whether today itself can be booked. Default true.

window_days.description: How far ahead a caller may book: from today (or tomorrow, without same_day) up to this many days after today. Default 30.

calls_from.description: The phone number this agent's outbound calls ring from when the call, or its campaign, does not choose one. Resolution is fixed: the call's (or campaign's) phone_number_id or pool_id, else this, else the workspace's default pool, else the workspace's own number, else the Mirai shared line (only for a workspace with no number that can place calls). A number set here dials through its own provider connection (India destinations only) and is re-checked before every call: if it can no longer call, calls fail with 409 not_ready and campaigns pause, never falling back to the shared line. null unsets it. Kept across a rollback.

phone_number_id.description: The id of one of your phone numbers (GET /v2/phone-numbers). It must be ready to call from: set up, on a verified connection and, for a rented number, inside its paid term. Empty or null unsets it.

draft.description: Drafts may have empty prompt or greeting, but cannot run calls.

emit_processed_webhook.description: Send call.processed when this agent has post-call tools, analysis or a flow (a flow agent's event carries the call's flow outcome). Set false to turn the event off.

features.description: Per-agent switches for platform behaviour still being tuned, by name. Each reaches the worker as a call variable of the same name, under the call's own variables: a variable the call supplies wins for that call. A switch the agent does not name keeps the platform's setting. Optional; {} or null clears every switch, and a PATCH replaces the whole object.

call_budget_secs.description: How long this agent's calls usually last, in seconds, for llm_timeline voice's time-left cue (60 when not set). A whole number from 20 to 3600; a JSON number or its digits as a string.

llm_timeline.description: on: each request to the reply model ends with the call's timeline (when each of the last six turns started, how long it ran, the silence before it) and the call time now. voice: the same, plus plain-word cues when they apply (the caller cut the agent off, keeps asking, answers slowly, has gone quiet, how much of call_budget_secs is left). Not on node flows or realtime sessions.

repeat_counter.description: on: the reply model is told what the caller has already heard the agent say several times on this call, so it words it differently. shadow: counted and logged, nothing sent. Not on node flows or realtime sessions.

tts_repeat_vary.description: on: a sentence the caller already heard on this call is rendered fresh, a little faster or slower, instead of replaying the same audio. A JSON boolean is accepted (true is on).

tts_rhythm.description: How each sentence is paced, on our own voices. on: our rules (a routine line flows quicker, a value read back to the caller slower, with pauses where a person recalls it). llm: the reply model starts a sentence with [slow] or [fast], never spoken. off: the voice as it comes.

turn_bc_choice.description: With adaptive interruptions: on, the turn model chooses the short word the agent says while the caller pauses ("जी", "हाँ"). shadow: asks and logs, and says today's word.

turn_fusion.description: With adaptive interruptions: on, the voice-end score and the turn model decide together when the caller has finished (a low score holds a reply, a high one answers at once). shadow: logs what it would have done.

flow.description: Optional node graph; makes this a flow agent. PATCH replaces the whole graph; null removes it.

if_revision.description: PATCH only: reject a stale update with 409.

anyOf.description: Root object schema from the documented bounded subset. Nested nodes use the same keywords; the server validates depth, node count and keyword/type compatibility.

additionalProperties.description: Nested schema node; same supported subset.

input_schema.description: Replace the entire input declaration. Null removes it and restores legacy string variables.

post.description:
Rings `to` and runs `agent_id` on the call. **This rings a real phone and uses wallet credit.** It answers **202** once the call is accepted. The phone hasn't rung yet, so poll [Get call](/api-reference/calls/get-call), take the webhooks sent to `webhook_url`, or follow it live: `events_url` is the call's live event stream (see [Stream live events](/api-reference/calls/stream-live-events)), with its own read-only token, so you can open it from a browser without your key.

Before your company goes live, every call runs and is billed at t5 (₹5 a minute, in 10-second blocks), whatever tier you send. The wallet must cover one minute before anything is dialled, or you get a 402 and nothing is charged.

**Idempotency-Key** keeps a retry to one phone call. The same key within 24 hours replays the first 202 (with `Idempotent-Replay: true`) and dials nothing. In your own code, build the key from your own record, like `order-8842-reminder-1`.

Everything but `agent_id` and `to` is optional:

* `variables` fill the placeholders in the agent's prompt and first message (up to 32, 512 characters each). Tools read them as `vars.*`.
* `metadata` is your own ids. They come back on the call and on every webhook, and the agent never sees them.
* `webhook_url`, `max_duration_secs` (30–1800), `first_message`, `timing`, `recording_enabled` and `final_results` work as the docs describe.
* `phone_number_id` calls from one of your own numbers (see *Phone numbers*) instead of the default route.

**A browser call instead:** see [Start a browser call](/api-reference/calls/start-a-browser-call): the same request with `"channel": "web"` and no `to`. `"channel": "realtime"` opens an OpenAI Realtime-compatible session the same way. Both are billed per minute like a phone call.

Optional for channel realtime: without it the session starts with an empty prompt, no tools, no greeting, the default voice and automatic language, and the Realtime client's session.update configures it. A realtime session never plays the agent's first_message; the client's first response.create starts the conversation.

An unknown key, an unknown voice or language is 400 invalid_request naming the allowed values. The effective values and their sources are on the call object as call_settings.

secondary_languages.description: Other languages callers may speak on this call. Base codes (gu-IN is read as gu; or as od); duplicates and the main language are dropped; at most 4. [] listens for the main language only.

voice_id.description: The voice the agent speaks in on this call: one of the voices an agent's voice.voice_id accepts, including your own custom voices (cv_...) except on channel realtime (422 voice_not_supported). Same as the older voice.voice_id; both with different values is 400.

channel.description: phone dials to; the answer adds events_url (live events). web is a browser session: no to, no route; the answer adds ws_url and events_url. realtime is an OpenAI Realtime-compatible session with the same rules, answer and per-minute price as web, except that it is refused (429 concurrency_limit) rather than queued when no voice slot is free; first_message, system_prompt, timing, test and flow agents are not accepted on it.

final_results.description: Send one consolidated call.processed after the call ends, once its transcript, any analysis or post-call tools and a flow agent's outcome settle, carrying data.transcript (and data.call.flow for a flow agent). Requires webhook_url.

first_message.description: Replaces the agent's opening line for this call only. {{var}} placeholders are substituted and validated like the agent's first_message. Not accepted for channel realtime.

metadata.description: Your own correlation ids (for example session_id, user_id). Frozen with the call and echoed unchanged in the call object and every webhook's data.call. Never given to the agent. Serialized size at most 4096 bytes. Do not put secrets here.

recording_enabled.description: Store the call's audio. Default true; a workspace whose policy disables recording defaults to false and answers true with 403 recording_disabled.

system_prompt.description: Replaces the agent's system prompt for this call only; the agent, its revision and every other setting stay the agent's. {{var}} placeholders are filled from this call's variables and validated like the agent's system_prompt (with an input_schema, each must be a declared input, a system variable or a pre-call tool output). Stored with the call but never returned on the call object or in webhooks. Not accepted for channel realtime (400 invalid_request) or for a flow agent (409 flow_system_prompt_unsupported). A sync pre_call tool may set the call's prompt instead (a top-level system_prompt string in its result, up to 48000 characters); one sent here wins over the tool's.

timing.description: Web and phone calls only (not realtime). Seconds count from live media start; max_duration_secs stays the hard cap. The *_before_end values must be at most the call's effective max_duration_secs minus 10, and close_secs_before_end less than wrap_up_secs_before_end when both are set.

variables.description: The agent's inputs for this call, checked against its input_schema (without one, string values only). Each value, as text (an object or array as its JSON), is at most 512 characters, except an input the agent's input_schema declares as an object, an array or a string with maxLength above 512, which may be up to 49152 characters. At most 65536 bytes in all. An over-long value is 400 invalid_request naming the key and its limit.

get.description:
What's happening on a call, as it happens, over [Server-Sent Events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events). Every call has it: phone calls (outbound, campaign and inbound), browser calls and realtime sessions.

**This response doesn't finish on its own.** It stays open and sends each event as it occurs: `agent.state` (listening, processing, speaking), `transcript.turn` for every completed turn, `turn.metrics` with how fast each agent reply came (`latency_ms` from the caller stopping to the reply's audio, and each stage's first-byte time), `tool.started` and `tool.completed` for each tool the agent runs during the call (names and timings, never arguments or results), `flow.node.entered` and `flow.variables.extracted` for a node-based agent, `language.changed` when the call switches language because the caller asked for another one or spoke it (and `language.not_enabled` when they asked for one the agent does not have), and finally `call.ended`, after which the stream closes.

Every event has an `id`. To resume after a drop, send it back as `after` (or as the `Last-Event-ID` header) and the stream carries on after that event. Events are kept for an hour after the call ends, so opening a finished call replays it and closes. A reader already past `call.ended` gets `204`.

A phone call's stream opens when it is placed and stays quiet while it rings; the first event arrives when the call is answered. A call that is never answered (busy, no answer) sends only `call.ended`, with the call's `status`.

Your API key works here, from your backend, for any call in your workspace. A browser should open the `events_url` that creating the call returned, which carries its own token, so your key never reaches the page. A campaign or inbound call has no create response, so read its stream with your key.

Steers a browser or realtime call while it is in progress. Send it from your backend.

* `{"type": "instruction", "text": …}` (1–1,000 characters) gives the agent a direction it follows from its next reply for the rest of the call. It isn't read aloud.

It answers **200** when the live call confirmed it within 3 seconds (`applied`, or `rejected` with a `reason`), and **202** with `status: pending` otherwise. Check a pending one with [Get a live control](/api-reference/calls/get-a-live-control). The call must be live: still `queued` (the page hasn't connected) or already ended is a `409 call_not_active`.

Send an Idempotency-Key. A repeat with the same key returns the same control and is never delivered twice, so a retry can't make the agent say goodbye twice.

post.description:
Tests a graph with simulated calls, reviews what happened, fixes what the review found and tests the fix. Nothing is saved. It answers 202 straight away with a job that usually finishes in 2–6 minutes: poll Get a flow test.

What to test with: `simulate` invented callers written from your `brief` (2 by default), `examples` (your real calls, each caller replayed against the graph), `calls` (transcripts of test calls you made), or a mix. `rounds` is the most revisions to make (1–3), and `verify` tests each revision again. `variables` are test values for the call variables. `agent_id` links the job to an agent so you can find it later.

Simulated calls are text only: no phone rings and no tool runs. This charges your wallet once, when the job ends, for every model call it made. 10 per workspace per hour.

schema.description: The graph to test and what to test it with: calls (test calls you made), simulate (simulated calls), or both. At least one test: with neither, 400 invalid_request.

agent_id.description: Optional: the agent this test is for, one of this workspace's agents (404 not_found otherwise). The job records it, and GET /v2/agents/{id}/flow/refinement answers the agent's latest job for 24 hours, so a client can let the test run on in the background.

brief.description: Optional: the business's requirements for the agent (the brief it was generated from). The review judges the flow against it and a revision keeps to it. Treated as data, never as instructions to the API.

calls.description: Optional: 1-5 transcripts of test calls you made with this flow, one AGENT:/CALLER: turn per line (POST /v2/agents/flow/transcribe turns a recording into one). The review reads them as real calls (speech recognition errors are not held against the flow); a revision is verified by replaying each call's caller against it.

transcript.description: One call, one turn per line: AGENT: (the agent) or CALLER:. At least one turn.

examples.description: Optional: transcripts of the business's real calls (2-10, together at most 200,000 characters), as given to generate. Their callers are replayed against the flow (simulate), and the review checks each replay against its original: coverage, order and what the original agent did well.

transcript.description: One call, one turn per line: AGENT: (the business's side) or CALLER:.

flow.description: The graph to test, as GET /v2/agents/{id}/flow or POST /v2/agents/flow/generate returns it. Validated like PUT /flow (400 invalid_flow).

language.description: Optional language code or name for the spoken lines (for example hi, gu, en or Hinglish). Without it the language is read from the brief, the example calls and the flow under test and your test calls (the Indian script they are written in, a language they name, or a language they are typed in with English letters), plain English text with no Indian words reads as English, and with nothing to go on no language is set and the brief decides, as before. Every Indian language is written in its own script (Gujarati in Gujarati script, Hindi and Marathi in Devanagari, and so on), English words in Latin letters, never romanized: text-to-speech reads Latin letters with English sounds.

max_duration_secs.description: Optional: the agent's call time limit. The review flags a main path that cannot finish inside it.

model.description: The model that reviews the test calls and revises the graph: gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini 3.8 Flash), claude-opus-5.5 (Claude Opus 5.5) or gpt-6-sol (GPT-6 Sol). Omitted: gemini-3.8-flash. Simulated calls do not run on it: both sides run on the model your tier's live calls run on (falling back to gemini-3.8-flash when that is unavailable).

rounds.description: The most revisions to make. Default 1: test, review, revise once, then re-test and review the revision to report what remains.

simulate.description: Simulated calls in the first round. With examples they are REPLAYS of the examples (the original callers played again against this flow): by default every example up to 5, the most different first, and never more than there are examples. Without examples they are invented callers: 2 by default. With calls the default is 0 (the calls are the test). Every later round runs the same callers again, so before and after are comparable.

variables.description: Optional test values for the call variables the graph reads as {{name}} (each key at most 64 characters). Every simulated caller gets plausible synthetic values for the rest, consistent with the caller.

verify.description: Re-test the graph after each revision with the same simulated callers (and a replay of every real call's caller, at most 5 replays a round) and review it again; revise again while rounds remain. false: one review and at most one revision, not re-tested.

post.description:
Makes a **draft** campaign. Nothing rings until you start it.

Required: `name`, `agent_id`, `timezone`, `start_date`, `end_date` and `slots`. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` and slots are `HH:MM`, both in the campaign's own timezone; up to 4 slots, and a slot may cross midnight. Set the dates to the days you actually want to call. A campaign whose dates have passed finishes as soon as it starts.

Optional: `max_concurrent` (1–50, default 1), `retry_count` (0–5 retries after the first attempt, default 0), `re_attempt_period_secs` (60–86400, default 900), `max_duration_secs` (defaults to the agent's), `budget_paise` (leave it out for no cap), `webhook_url`, `skip_called_before` (skip numbers another campaign has already reached), `final_results` (default `true`: each call ends with one `call.processed` carrying the transcript, the results and the contact's metadata) and `tier` (defaults to your plan).

`contacts` is optional here: up to 1000 rows per request, each `{id?, phone, variables?, metadata?}`. `variables` fill the placeholders in the agent's prompt for that person, the same way they do on a single call. `metadata` is your own fields the agent doesn't need (a CRM id, a branch): kept with the contact and sent on each of its calls' webhooks, never given to the agent. Every campaign call's webhooks also name its `campaign_id` and `contact_id`. A bad row doesn't sink the upload. It comes back in `contacts_rejected` with its index, and the good rows are stored.

There is no idempotency key on this route. If a create times out, list your campaigns before you retry, or you may end up with two.

analysis.description: Replace the whole analysis block. Omit output_schema to remove structured extraction. Requires enabled=true to run.

enabled.description: Run the analysis after every call that connected; a call that never connected is skipped (not_connected). Default false. On the T1 plan, your workspace's insights setting decides this for each call instead.

output_schema.description: The shape of analysis.data: a root object schema from the documented bounded subset. Nested nodes use the same keywords; the server validates depth, node count and keyword/type compatibility. The model's data must satisfy it before the result is published. Not a template: placeholders are not rendered here.

additionalProperties.description: Nested schema node; same supported subset.

prompt.description: What the analysis should summarise or extract, in your words: the instruction the model reads beside the transcript. At most 2000 characters. {{variable}} placeholders render with the same rules as system_prompt: the call's variables (for example {{customer_name}}) and pre-call tool outputs as {{tool_name.key}}. A placeholder with no value renders empty. For example: Write the summary in {{summary_language}}.

success_criteria.description: How to decide success: true, false, or null when the conversation does not show it. At most 2000 characters. {{variable}} placeholders render with the same rules as system_prompt: the call's variables (for example {{customer_name}}) and pre-call tool outputs as {{tool_name.key}}. A placeholder with no value renders empty.

archived.description: Archive to block new calls; false restores availability subject to draft validation. Accepted call snapshots remain unchanged.

behavior.description: How the agent takes turns with the caller, and whether it knows the date. Always present; agents saved before this block existed read back with the defaults.

adaptive_interruptions.description: Turn-taking, on by default. The agent decides when the caller has finished speaking: it waits through mid-thought pauses with a short "hmm", ignores quieter voices in the background (someone else in the room), and picks up a line it was cut off on if the interruption turns out to be nothing. Turn it off for fixed rules only: the interruptions setting decides how many words cut the agent off, and pass_through words never do.

date_awareness.description: Date awareness, on by default. The agent knows today's date in the call's timezone (the campaign's, else India), and whenever the caller names a day ("Saturday", "शनिवार", "15 तारीख", "कल", "next Monday", "15 November") it is told the exact date before it replies, so it never works out a date or a weekday itself. A day that does not exist (31 November) is flagged to the agent, and each resolved date is a row in the agent's Logs (prompt). Turn it off only if your own prompt or tools supply dates differently.

interruptions.description: How easily the caller can cut the agent off while it speaks. easy: one word or about 0.5 s of speech; normal (the default, and the behaviour before this setting existed): two words or about 0.7 s; firm: three words or about 1.2 s; never: the agent always finishes its line, and what the caller said is answered right after. Acknowledgements (haan, ji, ok, hmm and your pass_through words) never interrupt at any setting; a stop word (stop, ruko) interrupts at every setting except never. On a flow agent a node's own allow_interrupt false still applies; never makes every node non-interruptible. Trimmed and lower-cased; any other value, including an empty string, is 400.

pass_through.description: Your own words that never interrupt the agent, such as "theek", "achha" or "bilkul". They are added to the built-in acknowledgements (haan, ji, ok, hmm and their equivalents), which always pass through; a reply made only of these words does not stop the agent. Applies whether adaptive_interruptions is on or off. Each entry is literal text, never a pattern: Unicode-normalised (NFC), trimmed and inner spaces collapsed to one, then 1-40 characters and at most 4 words. Duplicates are removed ignoring case, keeping the first spelling and the order; at most 30 entries. Always returned: [] when there are none, including on agents saved before the field existed.

booking.description: The agent's booking window: which days a caller may book. With date awareness on, every day a caller names is marked as bookable or not before the agent replies (after the window, a closed weekday or date, already past), the agent is told the window in its prompt and offered the nearest bookable day, so it never confirms a day you cannot take. Absent when not set. A PATCH replaces the whole block (omitted fields take their defaults); null removes it. Present only on agents that have one.

closed_dates.description: Single days that cannot be booked, such as holidays, as YYYY-MM-DD. Saved unique and sorted; at most 100.

closed_weekdays.description: Days of the week that cannot be booked, lower case. Saved unique and in week order; closing all seven is 400.

same_day.description: Whether today itself can be booked. Default true.

window_days.description: How far ahead a caller may book: from today (or tomorrow, without same_day) up to this many days after today. Default 30.

calls_from.description: The phone number this agent's outbound calls ring from when the call or its campaign does not choose one; null when unset (the workspace's default pool, else its own number, else the Mirai shared line).

draft.description: Drafts may have empty prompt or greeting, but cannot run calls.

emit_processed_webhook.description: Send call.processed when this agent has post-call tools, analysis or a flow (a flow agent's event carries the call's flow outcome). Set false to turn the event off.

features.description: The switches this agent sets, as the worker reads them: every value a string (call_budget_secs as its digits). Always returned: {} when there are none, including on agents saved before the field existed.

call_budget_secs.description: How long this agent's calls usually last, in seconds, as digits.

llm_timeline.description: on: each request to the reply model ends with the call's timeline (when each of the last six turns started, how long it ran, the silence before it) and the call time now. voice: the same, plus plain-word cues when they apply (the caller cut the agent off, keeps asking, answers slowly, has gone quiet, how much of call_budget_secs is left). Not on node flows or realtime sessions.

behavior.description: How the agent takes turns with the caller, and whether it knows the date. Unlike other nested blocks, PATCH merges it field by field: omitted fields keep their current value and {} changes nothing; a sent pass_through replaces the whole list. null resets it to the defaults (interruptions normal, adaptive_interruptions true, pass_through [], date_awareness true).

adaptive_interruptions.description: Turn-taking, on by default. The agent decides when the caller has finished speaking: it waits through mid-thought pauses with a short "hmm", ignores quieter voices in the background (someone else in the room), and picks up a line it was cut off on if the interruption turns out to be nothing. Turn it off for fixed rules only: the interruptions setting decides how many words cut the agent off, and pass_through words never do.

date_awareness.description: Date awareness, on by default. The agent knows today's date in the call's timezone (the campaign's, else India), and whenever the caller names a day ("Saturday", "शनिवार", "15 तारीख", "कल", "next Monday", "15 November") it is told the exact date before it replies, so it never works out a date or a weekday itself. A day that does not exist (31 November) is flagged to the agent, and each resolved date is a row in the agent's Logs (prompt). Turn it off only if your own prompt or tools supply dates differently.

interruptions.description: How easily the caller can cut the agent off while it speaks. easy: one word or about 0.5 s of speech; normal (the default, and the behaviour before this setting existed): two words or about 0.7 s; firm: three words or about 1.2 s; never: the agent always finishes its line, and what the caller said is answered right after. Acknowledgements (haan, ji, ok, hmm and your pass_through words) never interrupt at any setting; a stop word (stop, ruko) interrupts at every setting except never. On a flow agent a node's own allow_interrupt false still applies; never makes every node non-interruptible. Trimmed and lower-cased; any other value, including an empty string, is 400.

pass_through.description: Your own words that never interrupt the agent, such as "theek", "achha" or "bilkul". They are added to the built-in acknowledgements (haan, ji, ok, hmm and their equivalents), which always pass through; a reply made only of these words does not stop the agent. Applies whether adaptive_interruptions is on or off. Each entry is literal text, never a pattern: Unicode-normalised (NFC), trimmed and inner spaces collapsed to one, then 1-40 characters and at most 4 words. Duplicates are removed ignoring case, keeping the first spelling and the order; at most 30 entries. Sent, it replaces the whole list; [] or null clears it. Anything else is 400 invalid_request naming behavior.pass_through.

booking.description: The agent's booking window: which days a caller may book. With date awareness on, every day a caller names is marked as bookable or not before the agent replies (after the window, a closed weekday or date, already past), the agent is told the window in its prompt and offered the nearest bookable day, so it never confirms a day you cannot take. Absent when not set. A PATCH replaces the whole block (omitted fields take their defaults); null removes it.

closed_dates.description: Single days that cannot be booked, such as holidays, as YYYY-MM-DD. Saved unique and sorted; at most 100.

closed_weekdays.description: Days of the week that cannot be booked, lower case. Saved unique and in week order; closing all seven is 400.

same_day.description: Whether today itself can be booked. Default true.

window_days.description: How far ahead a caller may book: from today (or tomorrow, without same_day) up to this many days after today. Default 30.

calls_from.description: The phone number this agent's outbound calls ring from when the call, or its campaign, does not choose one. Resolution is fixed: the call's (or campaign's) phone_number_id or pool_id, else this, else the workspace's default pool, else the workspace's own number, else the Mirai shared line (only for a workspace with no number that can place calls). A number set here dials through its own provider connection (India destinations only) and is re-checked before every call: if it can no longer call, calls fail with 409 not_ready and campaigns pause, never falling back to the shared line. null unsets it. Kept across a rollback.

phone_number_id.description: The id of one of your phone numbers (GET /v2/phone-numbers). It must be ready to call from: set up, on a verified connection and, for a rented number, inside its paid term. Empty or null unsets it.
