description.description: What the template is for. The model reads it when choosing.

language.description: The template's language, as you label it (at most 35 characters). Returned with a selected template.

variables.description: Always returned; [] when the template takes none.

description.description: What this value should hold. The model reads it when filling the template.

AnalysisTemplateResult.description: The template the analysis chose. Present only when the call's agent revision had analysis.templates.

missing.description: selected only, always present: declared keys left unfilled.

variables.description: selected only, always present: the declared keys the conversation established.

AnalysisTemplates.description: Pick the follow-up message after the call and fill in its variables. Exactly one of items or fetch. Requires analysis.enabled true.

fetch.description: Read the catalog from your endpoint after every call. Rendered like a post_call HTTP tool's request; secrets as {{ secrets.name }}.

body.description: JSON; POST only. Omitted on a POST: {"agent_id","call_id","metadata"}.

headers.description: Request headers, at most 20. Values are templates, rendered like a post_call tool's request.

items_path.description: Dot path to the list, e.g. Data. Default: a top-level array, else the first array among templates, data, Data, items.

query.description: Query parameters, at most 20, URL-encoded. Values are templates, rendered like a post_call tool's request.

instructions.description: How to choose, in the business's words.

items.description: The catalog: 1-50 templates. Exactly one of items or fetch.

Call.description: Partial call response schema documenting additive fields; other existing call fields are retained.

calls_from_source.description: How an outbound phone call's number was chosen: request (the call's own phone_number_id, or its campaign's), agent (the agent's calls_from), pool (a phone pool picked it), own (nothing chose one, so the workspace's own number), shared (the Mirai shared line, only for a workspace with no number that can place calls; shared with other customers and showing as Mirai) or trunk (a Mirai line: one from a campaign's caller_ids, or the caller ID Mirai set up for your workspace's shared-line calls). Absent on inbound, web and WhatsApp calls.

campaign_id.description: The campaign that placed the call. Present on every view and event of a campaign call; absent on every other call.

channel.description: How the call was held: phone (dialled out, answered inbound, or a WhatsApp call), web (a browser session), text (the console's typed test chat) or realtime (a Realtime API session). The same vocabulary as GET /v2/calls/summary's by_channel. Present wherever created_at is.

contact_id.description: The campaign contact the call was to: the id you sent with the contact, or the one minted for it. Present wherever campaign_id is.

created_at.description: When the call was accepted (RFC 3339, UTC): the time GET /v2/calls orders by and its from/to filter on. Present on GET and list, and in data.call of the ending event (call.completed, call.failed, call.voicemail, call.aborted) and call.processed; not on call.queued or call.started. Absent only on a call stored without one.

from.description: Phone calls only. The number the call rang from: your phone number (phone_number_id), the campaign's caller ID, or the shared line the call was dialled through. Present once the call has been dialled, and on every event from call.started on; absent on web and realtime calls.

metadata.description: The metadata sent when the call was created — or, for a campaign call, the contact's metadata — echoed unchanged here and in every webhook's data.call. Never given to the agent. Absent when the call has none.

phone_number_id.description: The id of your phone number the call rang from or was answered on. Absent when it rang from the shared line.

transcript_status.description: pending until the call has ended and its transcript is settled; ready when GET /v2/calls/{id}/transcript returns turns; empty when nobody spoke or media never started; failed when the transcript was lost. Present on GET and list.

CallAnalysisValue.description: Analysis embedded on a call and in result/processed events. status preserves the legacy processing state; durable extraction adds state, generation and agent_revision when available. success is explicitly null when unknown.

status.description: Legacy processing status, preserved alongside durable extraction state.

CallCreated.description: 202 response of POST /v2/calls. Web calls and realtime sessions add the session credentials (ws_url and events_url); a phone call adds events_url. Both are paths the public edge makes absolute. transport names the channel of a web call or realtime session.

events_url.description: Live events (Server-Sent Events) path with a reusable read-only token, valid for the call's maximum duration plus one hour. Returned for phone calls, web calls and realtime sessions. An idempotent replay repeats it while the token is valid.

ws_url.description: Browser audio socket path with a single-use token. Expires at ws_url_expires_at (300 seconds). An idempotent replay repeats it only while the token is unused.

CallFlow.description: A flow agent's call outcome. Present on GET /v2/calls/{id}, GET /v2/calls and call.processed data.call once the call's flow report has arrived (normally within seconds of the call ending); absent before that and on every prompt agent's call.

final_node.description: Id of the node the call ended on. Absent when the flow never entered a node (for example, the call failed before media).

nodes_visited.description: Node names in the order each was first entered; [] when none.

status.description: How the flow ended: end_call (an endCall node was reached), user_hangup, user_idle_max_duration_exceeded, call_duration_exceeded, pipeline_error, voicemail_detected or system_cancelled. A value outside this list is passed through as sent; treat it as an ending you do not recognise. Absent while only a partial report has arrived.

tags.description: Call tags the flow recorded (the disposition, user_speech, tag_* extractions). Absent when there are none.

variables.description: Values the nodes' extraction_variables captured, by variable name, as the model extracted them; {} when none.

CallSettings.description: The voice and languages for this call only, over the agent's. Every key is optional; a key left out keeps the agent's value (or, on a campaign contact, the request's). The same object is accepted on POST /v2/calls, on a campaign contact and in a pre_call tool's result. An unknown key or a value that fails these rules is 400 invalid_request naming it.

language.description: The main language speech recognition listens for on this call, as an agent's language (for example hi, gu or en-IN).

secondary_languages.description: Other languages callers may speak on this call. Base codes (gu-IN is read as gu; or as od); duplicates and the main language are dropped; at most 4. [] listens for the main language only.

voice_id.description: The voice the agent speaks in on this call: one of the voices an agent's voice.voice_id accepts, including your own custom voices (cv_...) except on channel realtime (422 voice_not_supported). Same as the older voice.voice_id; both with different values is 400.

CallSettingsEffective.description: The voice and languages this call ran with, and who chose each. Present on every call admitted since per-call settings existed (GET, list and every webhook); absent on older calls.

sources.description: Where each value came from: agent (the agent's own), request (POST /v2/calls call_settings or voice.voice_id), campaign (the campaign contact) or pre_call:<tool name> (that pre_call tool's result).

CallSummary.description: GET /v2/calls/summary: this workspace's calls created in [from, to), or all of them when both are null. Every key is always present; counts are calls, one per call id.

by_channel.description: Calls per channel: phone (dialled out, answered inbound, or WhatsApp), web (browser sessions), text (the console's typed test chat) and realtime (Realtime API sessions). The call object's channel says which one a call is.

by_direction.description: Calls per direction. Browser, text and realtime calls are outbound.

duration_secs.description: The calls' duration_secs, summed. A call that never connected, or has not ended, adds 0.

from.description: The from you sent (inclusive), in UTC; null when you sent none.

to.description: The to you sent (exclusive), in UTC; null when you sent none.

total.description: Every call in the window, whatever its status. by_channel and by_direction each add up to it.

Condition.description: A condition gates a tool. Combinators all/any/not nest at most 8 deep; at most 64 comparisons. Fields are dotted paths into vars, call, now, tools, args (on_call) or analysis (post_call). secrets are not readable from a condition. A field that is missing at run time compares false.

all.description: True when every condition in the list is true.

any.description: True when at least one condition in the list is true.

field.description: Dotted path, e.g. vars.priority or tools.lookup.tier. Use .0 for the first item of a list.

op.description: The comparison. exists, not_exists, is_true and is_false take no value; in and not_in take an array.

value.description: A string, number or boolean; an array for in/not_in. Omitted for exists/not_exists/is_true/is_false.

Flow.description: A node graph: the conversation as nodes with their own instructions and transitions between them. See x-semantics.flow for the rules.

viewport.description: Editor camera. Any JSON; stored and returned as sent.

cost.description: What the generation cost, charged to the workspace wallet once as a flow_generation transaction: the provider-reported cost of every model round × ₹88 × 1.2 (a round the provider reported no cost for at the model's per-token rates), rounded up once to a paisa. A balance smaller than the charge is taken to zero, never below.

flow.description: The draft graph, defaults materialised. It passes every rule PUT /v2/agents/{id}/flow applies. Not saved.

flow_revision.description: The draft's flow revision: the same graph saved has the same revision.

id.description: The generation id: the reference of its wallet transaction (kind flow_generation). Quote it in a support request.

input_schema.description: The variables as an agent input_schema, ready to save beside the flow. Every variable a node reads is required.

language.description: The language the draft's spoken lines are written in, as a code (hi, gu, en, ta, …): read from its greetings and quoted lines, or the request's language when they do not say (empty when neither says) (a language name this API does not know is returned as sent). Use it for the agent's language.

rounds.description: Model calls the draft took: 1 when the first answer was valid, at most 3 (two repair rounds).

usage.description: The tokens every model round that answered used, summed (estimated at four bytes a token for a round the provider reported no usage for). The ledger row's quantity.

variables.description: Call variables: values the business supplies before the call, read by the graph as {{name}}.

animated.description: Editor field. Any JSON; stored and returned as sent.

condition.description: When to take it; given to the model as the function's description. Must not be blank.

label.description: The function name the model calls to take this transition. Unique among the source node's transitions.

source.description: A node id; not an endCall or the globalNode.

target.description: A node id; not the globalNode.

type.description: Editor field. Any JSON; stored and returned as sent.

evidence.description: The test and the lines that show it.

fix.description: The change to the graph that fixes it.

nodes.description: Ids of the nodes the fix changes.

severity.description: high: the call fails its purpose or the caller is re-asked, stuck or annoyed; medium: noticeably unnatural or fragile; low: polish (reported, never revised automatically).

FlowGenerateRequest.description: At least one of brief or examples.

brief.description: What the agent does, in plain language: who it talks to, what it says and asks, how each answer is handled, what to record and the language. Up to 20,000 characters, so a structured specification written elsewhere fits. Optional when examples are given. Treated as the request, never as instructions to the API.

examples.description: Example calls: transcripts of the business's real calls, to learn the flow from (POST /v2/agents/flow/transcribe turns a recording into one). 2-10 of them, together at most 200,000 characters. The brief wins where they disagree; personal data in them is never copied.

transcript.description: One call, one turn per line: AGENT: (the business's side) or CALLER:.

flow.description: Optional graph to revise, as GET /v2/agents/{id}/flow returns it. Validated like PUT /flow (400 invalid_flow). The draft keeps what the brief does not ask to change.

language.description: Optional language code or name for the spoken lines (for example hi, gu, en or Hinglish). Without it the language is read from the brief, the example calls and a flow being revised (the Indian script they are written in, a language they name, or a language they are typed in with English letters), plain English text with no Indian words reads as English, and with nothing to go on no language is set and the brief decides, as before. Every Indian language is written in its own script (Gujarati in Gujarati script, Hindi and Marathi in Devanagari, and so on), English words in Latin letters, never romanized: text-to-speech reads Latin letters with English sounds.

model.description: The model that drafts: gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini 3.8 Flash), claude-opus-5.5 (Claude Opus 5.5) or gpt-6-sol (GPT-6 Sol). Each is charged at the provider's cost plus 20% (its published per-token rates when the provider reports no cost). Omitted: gemini-3.8-flash.

position.description: Editor layout. Any JSON; stored and returned as sent.

type.description: startCall opens the call (exactly one); endCall ends it after its reply (at least one, no outgoing transitions); globalNode is a prompt prepended to every node with add_global_prompt (at most one, no transitions).

greeting.description: Exact line spoken on entering the node; the start node's greeting opens the call.

prompt.description: The node's instructions, including when to call each outgoing transition. {{variables}} are rendered per call.

tools.description: Names of this agent's on_call tools the node offers the model beside its transitions, in order. startCall and agentNode only; never end_call and never a transition label. Omitted when empty.

FlowRefineRequest.description: The graph to test and what to test it with: calls (test calls you made), simulate (simulated calls), or both. At least one test: with neither, 400 invalid_request.

agent_id.description: Optional: the agent this test is for, one of this workspace's agents (404 not_found otherwise). The job records it, and GET /v2/agents/{id}/flow/refinement answers the agent's latest job for 24 hours, so a client can let the test run on in the background.

brief.description: Optional: the business's requirements for the agent (the brief it was generated from). The review judges the flow against it and a revision keeps to it. Treated as data, never as instructions to the API.

calls.description: Optional: 1-5 transcripts of test calls you made with this flow, one AGENT:/CALLER: turn per line (POST /v2/agents/flow/transcribe turns a recording into one). The review reads them as real calls (speech recognition errors are not held against the flow); a revision is verified by replaying each call's caller against it.

transcript.description: One call, one turn per line: AGENT: (the agent) or CALLER:. At least one turn.

examples.description: Optional: transcripts of the business's real calls (2-10, together at most 200,000 characters), as given to generate. Their callers are replayed against the flow (simulate), and the review checks each replay against its original: coverage, order and what the original agent did well.

transcript.description: One call, one turn per line: AGENT: (the business's side) or CALLER:.

flow.description: The graph to test, as GET /v2/agents/{id}/flow or POST /v2/agents/flow/generate returns it. Validated like PUT /flow (400 invalid_flow).

language.description: Optional language code or name for the spoken lines (for example hi, gu, en or Hinglish). Without it the language is read from the brief, the example calls and the flow under test and your test calls (the Indian script they are written in, a language they name, or a language they are typed in with English letters), plain English text with no Indian words reads as English, and with nothing to go on no language is set and the brief decides, as before. Every Indian language is written in its own script (Gujarati in Gujarati script, Hindi and Marathi in Devanagari, and so on), English words in Latin letters, never romanized: text-to-speech reads Latin letters with English sounds.

max_duration_secs.description: Optional: the agent's call time limit. The review flags a main path that cannot finish inside it.

model.description: The model that reviews the test calls and revises the graph: gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini 3.8 Flash), claude-opus-5.5 (Claude Opus 5.5) or gpt-6-sol (GPT-6 Sol). Omitted: gemini-3.8-flash. Simulated calls do not run on it: both sides run on the model your tier's live calls run on (falling back to gemini-3.8-flash when that is unavailable).

rounds.description: The most revisions to make. Default 1: test, review, revise once, then re-test and review the revision to report what remains.

simulate.description: Simulated calls in the first round. With examples they are REPLAYS of the examples (the original callers played again against this flow): by default every example up to 5, the most different first, and never more than there are examples. Without examples they are invented callers: 2 by default. With calls the default is 0 (the calls are the test). Every later round runs the same callers again, so before and after are comparable.

variables.description: Optional test values for the call variables the graph reads as {{name}} (each key at most 64 characters). Every simulated caller gets plausible synthetic values for the rest, consistent with the caller.

verify.description: Re-test the graph after each revision with the same simulated callers (and a replay of every real call's caller, at most 5 replays a round) and review it again; revise again while rounds remain. false: one review and at most one revision, not re-tested.

agent_id.description: The agent the request named, or null.

calls.description: The test calls the job was given, tidied to one AGENT:/CALLER: turn per line as they were tested; tests[].source.index (kind call) points into this list. Kept with the job (24 hours), readable only by its workspace; never logged.

changed.description: Once succeeded: whether flow differs from the graph sent.

cost.description: What the job costs: every simulated turn on the live-call model at the text channel's LLM rates (₹15 / ₹55 per million input / output tokens, the LLM API's rates), every hosted call (the callers, a fallback, the reviews and revisions) at the provider's reported cost × ₹88 × 1.2 (its per-token rates when none is reported), rounded up once to a paisa. So far while running; once finished (succeeded, failed or canceled), the amount charged to the wallet in one flow_generation transaction described "Flow test · <model> · … tokens".

examples.description: The example calls the job was given, as it used them, in order: a replay's tests[].source.index (kind example) points into this list, so a client can show each replay beside its original, and resending them with the current flow tests the same calls again. Kept with the job (24 hours), readable only by its workspace; never logged.

flow.description: Once succeeded: the final graph — the last valid revision, or the graph sent when nothing was changed (changed false). It passes every rule PUT /v2/agents/{id}/flow applies. Not saved.

flow_revision.description: Once succeeded: the final graph's flow revision.

found.description: What the first review found in the graph sent.

id.description: The job id (GET /v2/agents/flow/refine/{id}) and the reference of its wallet transaction (kind flow_generation). Quote it in a support request.

input_flow_revision.description: The flow revision of the graph the job was given (the graph under test).

input_schema.description: Once succeeded: the variables as an agent input_schema, ready to save beside the flow.

language.description: The language the flow's lines are written in, as a code (hi, gu, en, ta, …): while running, the one the job tests and revises in (the request's, else read from the brief, the calls and the flow; absent when they say nothing); once succeeded, the one the final flow's greetings and quoted lines are in. Absent on jobs started before it existed.

model.description: The model that reviews and revises.

progress.description: round: the test round under way (1-based); rounds: the most there can be (1, plus 1 per revision when verify is true: 2 by default); tests_done of tests_total: this round's tests.

remaining.description: What the last review found: with verify, in the final graph; without, in the graph sent.

rounds.description: The test rounds finished so far, in order.

simulation_model.description: The model simulated calls run on: the LLM your tier's live calls run on, as that stack names it (for example voice-agent), or gemini-3.8-flash when that model was unavailable, switched off or failed during the job (the job then falls back for good; each test names its model).

stage.description: What a running job is doing; done once it succeeded; where it stopped once it failed or was canceled.

status.description: canceled: stopped with POST /v2/agents/flow/refine/{id}/cancel; what had answered is charged and the rounds that finished are kept.

usage.description: Every model call's tokens, simulated turns included, summed. So far while running.

variables.description: Once succeeded: the call variables the final graph reads as {{name}}. When nothing changed, every one is typed string.

findings.description: What the review of these tests found, most severe first.

flow_revision.description: The revision of the graph these tests ran on.

revised.description: A revision was made from the high and medium findings; the next round tests it (or it is the result).

revision_issues.description: The revision stayed invalid after repairs, so the graph tested here was kept and the job stopped.

verdict.description: ready exactly when no high or medium finding remains.

ended.description: How a simulated call ended: an end node spoke its reply; the caller hung up; the agent spoke 20 times; the agent kept moving between nodes (4 transitions, or 8 function calls in one turn, without the caller speaking); or a technical failure cut it short (error says why). Absent for a real call.

estimated_secs.description: How long the call takes spoken: its words at about 150 a minute plus a second a turn.

kind.description: simulated: a text call with a simulated caller; real: one of the request's calls.

model.description: The model that played both sides of a simulated call: the live-call model, or gemini-3.8-flash after a fallback (a call the live-call model failed is run again from the start there). Absent for a real call.

nodes_visited.description: The names of the nodes a simulated call visited, in order; empty for a real call.

scenario.description: The simulated caller: who they are, what they want, how they act and speak, the call variables the call ran with (synthetic, and your variables) and, for a replay, the synthetic values that stood in for the original's redactions ([NAME] …).

source.description: Where the test comes from. kind example: a replay of examples[index]; kind call: calls[index] itself (a real test) or its caller replayed (a simulated test); kind invented: the index-th invented caller. index is 0-based.

transcript.description: The call in order. agent: the agent spoke (node_id/node_name: the node it spoke at; text may be empty when it said nothing); caller: the caller spoke; transition: the agent moved on (text: the function, node_id/node_name: the node it led to); tool: the agent asked for an on-call tool, which does not run in a test.

FlowTranscribeRequest.description: multipart/form-data. Send exactly one file part.

file.description: The call recording: at most 25 MB and 15 minutes. Common audio containers (mp3, mpeg/mpg, wav, m4a/mp4, ogg/opus, webm, flac, aac, amr). The audio is never stored.

language.description: Optional hint of the call's language (for example hi, en or Hinglish). The transcript keeps the language and script as spoken.

cost.description: What the wallet was charged: the provider-reported cost × ₹88 × 1.2, rounded up to a paisa.

duration_secs.description: The recording's length, to a tenth of a second.

id.description: The transcription id: the reference of its wallet transaction (kind flow_generation). Quote it in a support request.

transcript.description: One turn per line, each starting AGENT: (the business's side) or CALLER:. Personal data is replaced with [NAME], [PHONE], [ADDRESS] or [NUMBER]. Pass it as an examples[].transcript to POST /v2/agents/flow/generate.

usage.description: The tokens the model reported (the audio counts as prompt tokens; completion includes the model's reasoning).

Knowledge.description: Knowledge bases this agent answers from on calls (POST /v2/knowledge-bases). Available only on deployments where knowledge is enabled; elsewhere sending the block answers 400 knowledge_unavailable. Revisioned with the agent; a call pins the version of each base that is ready when it starts, and a base with no ready version yet is skipped. A PATCH replaces the whole block; null removes it.

base_ids.description: Up to 5 knowledge base ids from this workspace. An unknown or deleted id is 400 with its path.

max_chunks.description: Most passages given to the model per turn.

min_score.description: Relevance threshold from 0 to 1. null uses each knowledge base's calibrated threshold.

mode.description: auto puts a small knowledge base whole into the conversation and searches a large one every turn; always_retrieve always searches; off keeps the attachment without using it. tool is not available yet (400 knowledge_unavailable).

Tool.description: One tool on the agent. The minimum is a name, a phase and an https url; every other field has a documented default, and a saved agent reads them back materialised.

builtin.description: builtin tools only: the settings for this builtin. See GET /v2/tools/catalog.

description.description: on_call only: what the model is told the tool does.

enabled.description: false keeps the tool saved but never runs it. Default true.

execution.description: sync (default) or async, HTTP tools only. An async on_call tool runs in the background and returns its result when ready (timeout up to 300000 ms). An async pre_call tool starts with the pre-call phase and never holds the dial or the answer (timeout up to 120000 ms, on_failure continue): its outputs reach on_call tool requests, post_call tools and the analysis, and the live conversation as an instruction, once it answers.

kind.description: Inferred when omitted: builtin for a catalogued builtin name with no request, http otherwise.

name.description: Unique per agent. Becomes the tools.<name> namespace and, for an on_call tool, the function name the model calls.

on_failure.description: abort is pre_call only and means do not dial.

parameters.description: on_call only: JSON Schema for the model's arguments. Needs a tier whose model emits native tool calls (t3, t5); saving one on t1 returns 400 tool_style_unsupported.

phase.description: When the tool runs: pre_call before the call is placed or answered, on_call when the model asks for it during the conversation, post_call after the call ends.

request.description: http tools only. Every string is a {{ }} template over the phase's namespaces.

body.description: JSON template; a leaf that is exactly {{= path }} becomes the typed value. Not allowed on GET or DELETE. Omitted on an on_call POST/PUT/PATCH sends the model's arguments.

headers.description: Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding and Connection cannot be set.

url.description: https on port 443. Refused if it resolves to a private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast or metadata address, or to one of ours.

response.description: How the HTTP response becomes the tool's result and the values it promotes into variables.

select.description: Keys promoted into variables as <tool>.<key>, each at most 2048 characters.

strict.description: true makes a non-JSON body a failure instead of {"text": …}.

transform.description: jq, evaluated with a 100 ms budget and a 64 KB output cap. No input/inputs, no env, no modules. Paths start with a dot (.data.id, not data.id): a save refuses a transform it adds or changes that cannot compile. On a pre_call tool, a top-level call_settings object in the result (after transform) sets this call's voice and languages, and a top-level string system_prompt (at most 48000 characters) or first_message (at most 500) sets this call's system prompt or opening line, as a template whose {{var}} placeholders are filled from the call's variables and pre_call outputs (sync tools only; a request's own system_prompt or first_message wins; flow agents ignore them; a refused value is a receipt warning and never fails the call; never echoed on the call object; the receipt's call_prompt gives each one's length).

retry.description: Defaults 0 for pre_call and on_call, 2 for post_call. on_call may not retry: a second attempt is another whole timeout of silence for the caller.

attempts.description: Retries after the first attempt fails; 0 means one attempt only. The default and the maximum depend on the phase (see retry).

backoff_ms.description: Wait between attempts, in milliseconds. Default 500, at most 10000.

speak_while.description: on_call only: your own filler line, spoken while the tool runs. Empty means silence.

timeout_ms.description: Defaults and ceilings are per phase: pre_call 5000/15000, on_call 10000/30000, post_call 15000/60000.

when.description: on_call only: the WHEN rule appended to the system prompt.

Transcription.description: An offline transcription job. Lists carry the job without text, segments, draft or diarization; GET /v2/transcriptions/{id} adds them.

cost.description: Billing: pending until the job finishes; then charged once (₹18 per hour of audio, rounded up to a paisa) or free (degraded or failed). amount_inr is the job's charge at the rate frozen when it was accepted; the wallet transaction (kind transcription, reference = the job id) records what the balance moved.

degraded.description: Once completed: true when the merge step was unavailable, so text is a single decoding pass without speaker roles; a degraded job is free. null until completed.

diarization.description: Completed jobs, GET by id only.

non_speech.description: Parts of the recording that were not speech, such as ringing or a caller tune, and were left out of the transcript. Absent when nothing was left out.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the recording.

speakers.description: One entry per voice, in speaker_id order (spk0 first): the agent is spk0 and the customer spk1 on a call between them.

draft.description: While merging, GET by id only: the strongest single decoding pass, readable seconds after decoding and before the merge finishes. Speaker is empty. Replaced by segments once completed.

duration_s.description: The recording's length in seconds, known once decoding has started.

error.description: Why a failed job failed. transcription_failed and audio_too_long are the recording's fault (not audio, damaged, empty, or too long); every other code is a fault on our side, and the same recording can be submitted again. A failed job is free.

id.description: The job id; also the reference of its wallet transaction (kind transcription).

language.description: The language you forced, or null for automatic detection.

model.description: The model that produced the transcript, once completed (mira-transcribe-offline-1).

segments.description: Completed jobs, GET by id only.

status.description: queued → decoding → merging → completed | failed; there is no progress figure. A job typically completes in about 10 seconds plus 15% of the recording's length; diarization adds about a second.

text.description: The whole transcript; completed jobs, GET by id only.

TranscriptionRequest.description: application/json: a recording we fetch from an https url (public address, at most 200 MB, at most 2 hours of audio). Send the file itself as multipart/form-data instead (TranscriptionUploadRequest).

context.description: Optional: what the call is about (a business, a product, the purpose of the call). Helps the transcript spell names and terms right.

diarize.description: Speaker turns from the voices themselves: each segment gets a speaker_id (spk0, spk1, …) and a role. Adds about a second.

language.description: Optional: force the call's main language; auto (the default) detects it. Mixed-language speech is kept as spoken.

url.description: An https URL of the recording (for example a pre-signed storage link). Fetched once when the job is accepted; never stored or logged.

vocabulary.description: Optional: names, brands and terms to spell right — a string separated by commas or new lines, or an array of strings. At most 200 terms of 100 characters each.

words.description: Word timings on each segment, when the call aligns (Hindi calls; Gujarati and English calls get none).

speaker.description: The party: Agent, Customer or Other; empty when it could not be told (a degraded job, or the draft).

speaker_id.description: The voice, per recording (spk0, spk1, …). Agent voices are numbered first, then Customer voices, then any others, each in order of first appearance, so on a call between an agent and a customer the agent is spk0 and the customer spk1. Present when diarization was applied.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the recording.

words.description: Present when words was requested and the call aligned.

TranscriptionUploadRequest.description: multipart/form-data: the recording itself (at most 45 MB; send a larger one by url). Send exactly one file part; every other field is text.

context.description: Optional: what the call is about (a business, a product, the purpose of the call). Helps the transcript spell names and terms right.

file.description: The recording: any common audio format (wav, mp3, m4a, ogg, flac, webm, amr …), at most 2 hours. Deleted once it is decoded; never stored by the API.

language.description: Optional: force the call's main language; auto (the default) detects it. Mixed-language speech is kept as spoken.

vocabulary.description: Optional: terms separated by commas or new lines; at most 200 terms of 100 characters each.
